decision: Select typed observed commit for the explicit exclusive existing-key cold-write candidate on all three CPUs. Existing-primary growth improves; MM8 cold growth beats the fastest measured actual Abseil controls, including companion work. ARM MM64 still loses. Hot procedures should keep immediate/plain-prefetch choices; fitting appends still trail. Experimental global defaults remain off; fresh-key performance and public retained-reader composition remain unqualified.
limits: K30, 85% load; hot b10 and cold b19/MM8 or b17/MM64; 512 MiB cold conditioning, not proof of DRAM residence. Whole caller including priming, admission, allocation, ordered commits, paced independent companion reads and physical drain. Source setup/adoption and validation outside timing. Best-procedure minima are retrospective diagnostics, not an implemented oracle. Plain-prefetch whole-caller ratios are retained, including warm ARM MM64 regressions despite preserved immediate kernel closures.

reader_source_identity.scope: Baseline reader source identity between v43c and v44c only; v43c is invalid as selected-reader qualification. See observed-reader-preservation-v44d.json for the subsequent nontrivial preservation of all complete selected writer roots when actual selected-reader implementations are added.

protocol.mixed_pacing: Complete exactly one companion quantum after each128committed writes, and the final tail, before further writes. Other observation callbacks may progress during this service.
protocol.scope: Exclusive heap, accepted grants, no journal or retention service. Timing includes per-request binding, admission, priming, complete append including allocation, ordered commit, companion service and physical drain. Owner population, source generation, adoption, Runtime setup, conditioning and validation are outside. Mixed ns is total makespan divided by writes, also doing one independent read per write. Plain primary-only hints and multistage observation hints are distinct complete procedures, not isolated dispatch controls.
